title: TypeScript SDK: output contracts codegen with discriminator resolver and streaming-friendly retry semantics
creator: Evan Chen
description:
Problem: Current TypeScript SDK codegen for structured outputs produces compile-time types and Zod schemas, but we repeatedly see two production issues: 1) streaming responses with discriminated unions lose discriminator context across chunk boundaries, leading to incorrect incremental parsing and developer confusion; 2) retries (client-side or server-side reconnects) cause partial state to be reprocessed and the runtime validators are not idempotent, causing duplicate errors or brittle error messages.

Proposal: Generate a single "output contract" artifact per model schema that includes: static TypeScript types, Zod schema, JSON Schema (for external integrations), and a small runtime "discriminator resolver" with a streaming-aware parser. The resolver will: 1) accept partial JSON/token chunks and maintain minimal provenance (discriminator bytes and relevant keys) without eagerly materializing full objects; 2) expose a deterministic merge/rehydration API so that when a retry happens the parser can resume or reparse without producing spurious validation failures; 3) provide a small set of ergonomic helpers (parseChunk, finalize, replay) that map directly to the streaming SDK surface.

Implementation notes: codegen will be a new tsdx plugin invoked by the SDK build pipeline; it will emit a pair of files per schema: *.types.ts (types + doc comments) and *.contract.ts (zod schema, jsonschema, resolver). The streaming parser will be implemented as a tiny state machine (max ~200 LOC) that operates on token objects from the SDK's streaming layer (we already have token boundaries in the runtime). The parser will prefer lazy validation for large nested arrays and only validate discriminators eagerly.

Backward compatibility: existing API surface for sync structured output parsing remains supported; this work augments streaming parse with new API overloads and opt-in feature flag on the SDK (parseAsContract: true).

Why this path: generating companion runtime resolvers keeps runtime overhead predictable (small generated code per schema) and avoids shipping a heavy reflection/validator at runtime. Zod remains the canonical runtime validator for developer ergonomics and error messages; JSON Schema continues to be emitted for infra/contract tests and for downstream teams that rely on JSON Schema integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Codegen emits types + contract modules (.types.ts and .contract.ts) for the example schema used in the PR
Zod schema and JSON Schema produced match the static TypeScript types in shape (roundtrip tests added)
Streaming parser helpers (parseChunk, finalize, replay) available and covered by unit tests simulating chunked discriminator scenarios
Retry/rehydration path: when a simulated retry occurs mid-stream, the parser can replay buffers and produce identical final validated object without duplicate errors
Docs: examples added to docs/sdk/structured-output streaming README and a short migration guide for users
A real-world integration test using the chat->structured-output example demonstrates no regressions and improved error messages
PR merged and release note drafted for sdk-2026.03
comments: 2026-03-10 Evan Chen: Created ticket after pairing with product on recurring customer bug about streaming structured outputs dropping discriminator info.
2026-03-11 Sofia Patel: Spike completed — implemented toy resolver that handles discriminator-first streaming; initial perf looks good (sub-ms per chunk) and codegen seems straightforward.
2026-03-11 Marcus Green (review): Suggest we keep the public API minimal: expose parseStream(stream, contract) and not raw token hooks to reduce surface area.

decision_log: Generate companion runtime resolver vs. ship one runtime validator: chose per-schema generated resolvers to minimize runtime weight and give clearer, schema-local error messages.
Use Zod as canonical runtime validator for developer ergonomics and message quality; also emit JSON Schema for infra consumers.

Provide streaming-friendly API (parseChunk/finalize/replay) rather than exposing token internals. This keeps SDK surface stable and allows future runtime optimizations behind the parser implementation.
Opt-in flag parseAsContract: true for GA to preserve backward compatibility and give customers time to migrate.
Keep discriminator resolution eager but nested validations lazy to balance correctness and performance.
